newsitem.title: USA: Standard Federal says ABN offer was best.
newsitem.headline: Standard Federal says ABN offer was best.

text.p: Standard Federal Bancorp Inc said the acquisition proposal from Dutch bank ABN AMRO Holding NV to buy it for $1.95 billion, or $59 per share, was the highest offer.
It said as announced earlier, Charter One Financial Inc of Cleveland withdrew a November 22 proposal to merge with Standard Federal.

Standard Federal chairman Thomas Ricketts said Charter One and others took part in a formal process over several weeks, during which parties interested in acquiring Standard Federal submitted proposals.
"The proposal received from ABN AMRO North America Inc was the highest offer and was determined by Standard's board, and continues to be, the superior transaction," Ricketts said in a statement.
The company entered into definitive agreements with ABN AMBO late on November 21.
